title: Function-Preserving Audits of Visual Weight Readers
read_level: partial (PDF v2 via pdftotext: abstract, intro, related work, method, main results, discussion and the LLM generated-answer appendix H read; other supplementary tables skimmed)
metadata_mismatch: none (read version is v2, dated 13 Nov 2026; corpus date 2026-11-04 taken as first version)
why_wsp: Mainly audits learned weight-space readers (HiddenProbe, ProbeGen, set readers) of neural fields under function-preserving weight transformations; includes a 720-response study where LLMs (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol) read numerical field weights to classify shapes, with no weight editing.
domain: neural fields / implicit neural representations (shapes, MNIST, CIFAR10) and weight-space classifiers
editor: none for main study (learned readers); LLM readers: gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6-luna (high reasoning effort, no tools); next-token controls Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B-Instruct, SmolLM2-360M-Instruct, Qwen3.5-0.8B, Qwen3.5-27B
target: shallow ReLU fields and two-hidden-layer SIREN fields (exact sizes in supplement); HiddenProbe head 447,908 parameters
interface: other (LLMs read six-significant-digit decimal weights in a prompt; learned readers take weights/activations)

headline_results.quote: one-period hidden-bias shifts change 7.3% of a released HiddenProbe configuration’s predictions while barely changing accuracy; three-period shifts change 22.0% and reduce accuracy from 57.8% to 54.4%
a one-period shift of hidden biases changes 61.6% of HiddenProbe predictions even though the checked field discrepancy is at most 1.12 × 10−5
Shape Stats ridge falls from 96.7% to 24.2% under joint permutation and rescaling
complete canonical hidden features reach 38.7% on MNIST, whereas explicitly composing those activations, outgoing weights, and output bias into field outputs reaches 81.5%

headline_results.claim: LLM readers: accuracy loss under equivalent weights
headline_results.quote: Three independent responses per raw and joint input on 60 origins give Astra 88.3% versus 81.1% accuracy and Sol 86.7% versus 79.4%
original-input repeats already disagree on 13.3% and 16.7% of pairs, compared with 15.7% and 20.9% cross-input disagreement. Both exact response-distribution tests give Holm-adjusted p = 0.162
Qwen2.5-0.5B gives the same letter on all 60 original and redacted inputs. A Qwen3.5-27B control reads 7/60 weight inputs but 60/60 explicit cues

baselines_and_controls: Output-query reader (ProbeGen) as function-only reference; matched phase-wrapping (HiddenPhase) and sign-invariant (HiddenGram) controls; canonicalization; augmentation; for LLMs: original-input repeats, redacted weights, explicit shape cues, randomized answer menus.
runs_and_variance: Readers: 5-6 seeds for feature-location and canonical studies; Wilson intervals and class-stratified origin bootstraps (2,000 or 10,000 resamples). LLMs: 1,920 exploratory responses (4 configs x 60 origins x 8 conditions) plus prospective 720 (3 raw + 3 joint per origin, Astra and Sol), pre-fixed Holm family.
robustness_of_edits: n/a (no edits); robustness of readers to function-preserving transformations is the object of study
verification: Numerical verification that transformed fields match (max full-precision ReLU discrepancy 1.8e-15; exact-rational bounds for decimal-serialized inputs); exact conditional permutation tests for stochastic readers.
memorization_vs_reasoning: LLM readers lose accuracy under equivalent reparameterizations (Astra 88.3% to 81.1%), i.e. some dependence on parameter coordinates, but the exact tests do not reject response-law equality given repeat variability; paper says nonrejection "does not establish invariance".
limitations_stated: Scope limited to shallow ReLU and two-hidden-layer SIREN fields; mechanistic repairs use adapted readers; one released configuration per method; unequal capacity in feature-location comparisons; generated-answer tests assume independent stationary calls and have limited power at three repeats per side.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al., Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog, 2026)
notes_for_survey: Methodological evaluation paper: argues weight-reader audits (including LLM readers) should test function-preserving reparameterizations with numerical verification and, for stochastic readers, repeats on both inputs. LLM part is small (60 origins, two configs prospective) and finds accuracy drops that are not statistically separable from repeat noise.
